newsitem.title: USA: Miami oversight board seeks data on arena cash.
newsitem.headline: Miami oversight board seeks data on arena cash.

text.p: A state oversight board has asked Miami for more details on a proposal calling for the Miami Sports and Exhibition Authority to give the city $12.9 million to help Miami balance its budget, the Miami Herald said Wednesdsay.

Specifically, the board demanded that the city provide data on what it is obliged to pay for renovations and upkeep at the Miami Arena. The authority acted as a funding conduit for the arena, issuing revenue bonds backed by hotel bed taxes.

The arena board and Dade County have already agreed to give the city $12.9 million that the authority holds in reserves. But the deal still must be approved by the oversight board, which asked for details by Friday.
"We need to see that other city obligations -- i.e. the arena -- don't fall to the wayside," oversignt board member Cynthia Curry said.
Lawyers for the Decoma Miami Associates, the arena management company, said the money must be set aside for capital improvements and other obligations of the arena.

But lawyers for the authority and the city said the only restriction on the money is that it must be used for tourism-related expenses, which means the city could use that money instead of general fund revenues for costs such as the city convention center.
The cash infusion is part of a plan to eliminate Miami's $68 million deficit for the budget year that began Oct 1. The oversight board has until Jan. 20 to approve a plan.
